newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares surge as Maof index reaches record.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares surge as Maof index reaches record.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply higher in extremely heavy trading on Monday with the Maof index of blue chips reaching an all-time high, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 2.85 percent, or 7.10 points, to 256.04 on very high all-share turnover of 260 million shekels against 175 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 3.21 percent higher at 265.63.
"This is a real madness. The market is rising without taking any rest. I believe that in the near future we will see a sharp correction," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.
"The demand for shares is growing and the supply is very limited....Activity is also improving and the mood is positive," added Dan Galai of Sigma Securities.

"Many Maof shares are over-valued now and investors are still buying. Despite that, many small- and medium-capitalisation stocks are still very attractive and the outlook for the stock market is very positive," Scharia said.

Galai said that in the long run the trend is expected to remain positive as investors expect that the Bank of Israel will continue to lower its key lending rate. "But in the short run we might see a correction," Galai added.

Tadiran surged 6.25 percent to 9,770 agorot, which analysts said followed a report in the newspaper Haaretz that investor George Soros had been buying Tadiran shares. Haaretz quoted a report appearing in the U.S. magazine Barron's.

A research report released on Monday by Zannex Securities downgraded Tadiran to a long-term buy from a strong buy. Zannex lowered its 12-month target price for Tadiran to 1,040-1,130 agorot because of lower sales growth than previously forecasted.
Israel Chemicals, the third active share, rose 4.0 percent to 369 agorot on volume of 10.2 million shekels. In a report released on Monday Ofek Securities and Investments rated the company a buy.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which gained 3.75 percent to 34,217 agorot on volume of 15.3 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which surged 4.0 percent to 648 agorot on turnover of 13.8 million shekels.
